_about: The art methods the Level Editor offers (pass 66, lane B). Lane V draws the method cards from `methods`, lane P builds the recipe rows from `recipe_fields`, lane J maps `runner`. Times are medians measured on disk (see timings_note). `kind` is enemy (creatures and bosses), hero, item, or driver / ref for the 3D-reference tools. A `recipe_fields` key with a dot (pose_drivers.back) is a path into a nested object of the recipe; `job_fields` are the job's own settings (flags, pre-steps), not recipe keys. In `runner.argv`, {x} is a value from the target or a field, and a token ending in ? is sent only when its field is set or true; `call: blender` means `$BLENDER -b --python tools/<tool>.py -- <argv>`.

methods.name: Hero: five views on a Mixamo stride
methods.summary: Klein paints the front still from your words with the style anchor as its reference, then edits that painting into the back, the side, the two diagonals, a cheer, five hurt faces, a dead pose and a portrait (13 stills, about 20 s each). Wan Animate then walks each of the five view stills on an OpenPose driver (the run driver, or the one the recipe names per view), one sprite frame per driver frame, 24 a view, so every view shares one cadence. The hit is four frames round the hurt still, the death the front flinch tipping into the dead still; the strip is packed and, for the hero's base look, the round badge painted. A new look paints stills of its own (cached as <id>_<letter>_<view>, with seeds of its own), so a Duplicate never comes out as its source; a look made from the hero's own paintings keeps them (stills ''). You pick nothing while it runs; afterwards you look at every still and clip and re-roll one still (its key and a seed) or one clip (its folder moves aside and anim_seed goes up by one).
needs: the style anchor (game/art/style/style_anchor.png)
OpenPose driver folders under tools/dl/drivers (run by default, 24 frames; others per view through pose_drivers)
methods.produces: 13 stills, 5 clips of 24 frames, a strip of 166 frames (62 columns), the round badge (base look only)
weaknesses: A face gets painted on a back cycle (the QA re-rolls it; look at the back clip yourself).
Hands painted through the torso on the back views: give the back and bd views the run_occ or run_spread driver.

A wide figure that touches the clip's edge falls back silently to a free clip and run_fps drops to 14: shrink the driver (pose_scale 0.85) or set clip_fill 0.56; the result's clip_kind says which clips fell back.
Klein draws running figures smaller, and a hero whose proportions are not a man's (a big head on a slim body) gets a different head size per view: fit the driver to the painting (hero_fit).
The vision QA cannot count fingers, arms or ears: paint several seeds and pick by eye.
anim_negative does nothing at Wan Animate's cfg 1.0; the seed and the driver are the levers.
A hurt still painted from the back view sometimes turns to face front: hurt stills are edits of each view's own still, check them.

recipe_fields.help: Who the hero is: the words the front still is painted from, with the style anchor. A look's recipe may override the hero's own.

Added to the seed of every clip: re-rolls the clips while the paintings stay (only a clip whose folder was moved aside rolls again).

Per-view size of the run / walk clips (pass 70, lane ART's gen_art key): 1 = as fitted. gen_art fits every view's walk by its tallest frame to the standing height, so a view that crouches in every frame (a side run) comes out taller than the others and one whose foot reaches toward the camera (a back or front run) smaller; a driver scaled with + Tweak a driver… cannot fix that (it is fitted back). 0.88 = 12 % smaller; clamped 0.5..1.5. A re-queue re-places the cached walks: nothing is painted again. A view grows only while its tallest frame fits the cell: shrink the others instead.

methods.name: Hero: another walk, fitted to this painting
methods.summary: The same hero on other drivers: nothing is painted again (the stills are cached by their keys, and still_keys may swap single paintings for composed ones), only the five clips roll, on the driver the recipe names per view. Before them the pre-step jobs make the fitted driver: pose_fit scales the stick figure to the painted body and pins the face on the painted head (it needs a template measured on the still, tools/pose_templates/<id>.json), pose_spread pushes the back views' wrists out past the torso, pose_scale shrinks the back views so wide arms stay inside the clip, pose_occlude hides the hand that swings in front of the chest. You choose the source driver and the steps, then look at the five clips.
needs: the hero's stills already painted (hero_pose5 ran once)
a source driver folder; for pose_fit a template tools/pose_templates/<id>.json measured on the front still
methods.produces: 5 clips of 24 frames, the strip <id>_sprite_<letter>.png (the badge and the title cut-out are the hero's and are not redone)
weaknesses: The template is hand-measured today (Solenne's is the only one): a new hero needs its own before pose_fit does anything.
A look never redoes the badge or the title cut-out: those belong to the hero.

Wan paints the figure on the driver's bones: an unfitted driver makes the head bigger walking down and smaller walking up, and the hands large (the Mixamo body was a third taller than Solenne's painting).
A walk with the toes turned out reads its forward off the feet up to 20 degrees wrong: the driver wants fwd=body.
Klein will not turn some heads (Solenne's sun disc came out edge-on six times out of six): compose the still and name it in still_keys.

methods.name: Hero: a 3D puppet of the painting walks him (the Puppet method)
methods.summary: The look's painting becomes a rigged 3D figure whose own renders guide the video model instead of a flat Mixamo stick figure. Klein (or Flux.2 dev) edits the source look's front still into an arms-out A-pose (candidates: you pick one on the job card), then the side and the back the same way (or you give a look's still or an uploaded picture per view; side and back may be left out); Hunyuan3D-2mv makes the 3D shape from them on the AI server through ComfyUI's own nodes (two tries: you pick one); Blender cleans it, finds the joints, rigs it with Mixamo's bone names and automatic weights, plays the Mixamo clip on it (running.fbx by default, the idle procedural or a Mixamo idle), colours it from the paintings and exports the GLB you can turn and play in the editor; then the guides: OpenPose stick figures from its own bones (framed by the soles, the joints its body hides dropped), depth videos of its run and its silhouette (how tall its run stands against its idle in each view). The look walks on them: the depth views by Wan 2.2 Fun Control, the others by Wan Animate on the stick figure, each view sized by the puppet's own run/idle height (run_fit, no run_scale to tune), on the source look's stills (nothing painted again) or stills of its own. A hero who has a puppet starts the next look from it (no shape, no rig: the walks only), or from his .blend after you moved a joint, or from a Mixamo-rigged FBX.
needs: a hero look with front, side and back stills (the source look: the one he is played in by default)
Hunyuan3D-2mv in the AI server's models/checkpoints (hunyuan3d-dit-v2-mv.safetensors, 4.9 GB; there since the trial)
Blender 5.2 on this PC; a Mixamo clip in tools/dl/mixamo/ (running.fbx by default)
methods.produces: tools/dl/puppet/<hero>/: the arms-out paintings, shape.glb, <hero>_puppet.blend (mesh <Name>, armature <Name>_Rig, Mixamo bones), <hero>_puppet.glb (clips run and idle) and its preview; tools/dl/drivers/<hero>_puppet_<clip>[_N] (OpenPose, silhouette.json) and _depth; then the look's strip of 166 frames like hero_pose5's
weaknesses: Hunyuan3D-2mv's licence (the Tencent Hunyuan 3D 2.0 Community License) does not cover the European Union, the United Kingdom or South Korea: Garry accepted it for this project; read it again before anything made with it ships from there. The 3D model only guides the walk (the sprites are still Wan's paintings).

The AI server's card is an AMD R9700 (ROCm): Hunyuan3D runs through ComfyUI's built-in nodes only (no custom 3D nodes, no Hunyuan3D-Paint textures); ComfyUI is restarted before and after it because the server's RAM is tight, so the comfy lane pauses for about 30 s twice.

A depth video carries no face: Fun Control painted a crosshatched face, then long hair, on May's front; walk the front on the puppet's stick figure (the default) and name the hair and the face in anim_hint for the views that show them.
The arms must stand clear of the body in the 3D reference: a still with hanging arms fuses them into the torso and the rig cannot free them. Paint arms-out (the default) or give an arms-out picture.
Klein's arms-out candidates sometimes have four hands or a near T-pose (Jeżyk's c1 had four hands): pick by eye.
The colours are the paintings projected onto the mesh: what no painting saw (under the arms, the soles) takes the nearest seen colour. The GLB is a guide for the video model, not a game asset.
The walks can show rainbow fringes on the sleeves and boots: "Clean colour fringes" (on by default) turns them into the painting's own colours.
The idle is procedural (arms down, a breath, a sway) unless a Mixamo idle is put in tools/dl/mixamo/.
A side run painted May's face to the camera until the guide's ear sat ahead of the neck (fixed in the guides): look at every view's walk against its idle anyway.

A depth video cannot tell a front from a back: MAY-R's first back walk, on a hint that described her face for the front, ran facing the camera. "Keep the face angle" (on by default) walks the back views on words without the face; look at the back walk anyway and re-roll that one view if it faces you.

recipe_fields.help: Size from the 3D model: each view's walk stands as tall as the 3D model's run stands against its idle in that view (by the middle frame), not its tallest frame stretched to the standing height. Prevents a crouching side run coming out taller than the others. On by default; the job writes run_fit below from it.
recipe_fields.label: Size from the 3D model

recipe_fields.help: Frame by the soles: the stick figures sit in the canvas measured from the lowest sole, so chunky boots stay inside the picture (MAY-P's front left the canvas on the ankle framing). soles by default.
recipe_fields.label: Frame by the soles

recipe_fields.help: Clean colour fringes: colours the view's painting does not have (rainbow fringes on sleeves and boots) turned into its nearest own colour. On by default; the job writes fringe_remap below from it.
recipe_fields.label: Clean colour fringes

recipe_fields.help: Keep the face angle: the stick figures' ears are placed from the 3D model's measured nose, so a side view stays in profile (head = on the head bone: May's side run turned its face to the camera), and the back and back-diagonal views walk on words without the face (a depth video cannot tell a front from a back: MAY-R's first back walk faced the camera). nose by default.
recipe_fields.label: Keep the face angle

recipe_fields.help: Depth or stick figure: the views walked on the depth video (Wan Fun Control: the body's own shape, no face); the others on the stick figure (Wan Animate, with the face points). Keep the front on the stick figure: the depth video has no face.
recipe_fields.label: Depth or stick figure (depth views)

recipe_fields.label: Source look

recipe_fields.help: The walks' stills: reuse the source look's (nothing painted again) or paint this look's own.

recipe_fields.help: Start from: auto = the puppet he has (what is on disk is kept); fresh = a new puppet (the old one moved aside); blend = his .blend after you changed the rig; fbx = a Mixamo-rigged FBX.
recipe_fields.label: Start from

recipe_fields.label: Moving clip

recipe_fields.help: The idle clip (a Mixamo FBX in tools/dl/mixamo/); empty = the procedural idle (arms down, a breath, a sway).
recipe_fields.label: Idle clip

recipe_fields.label: Arms-out painter

recipe_fields.help: The 3D reference per view: paint (arms-out, painted locally), still:<key> (a look's still), a picture's path, or none (side/back).
recipe_fields.label: 3D reference per view

recipe_fields.help: Written by the job after the guides from "Size from the 3D model": the 3D model's silhouette.json (each view's run against its idle). Empty = the tallest frame fitted (run_scale's way).
recipe_fields.label: run_fit (written by the job)

recipe_fields.help: Written by the job from "Clean colour fringes": gen_art turns the clips' colours the painting lacks into its own.

Words to avoid in the clips (Fun Control reads them; Wan Animate at cfg 1.0 does not).

Added to the seed of every clip: re-rolls the walks while the stills stay.

methods.name: Creature: front and back, Wan guesses the walk
methods.summary: Klein paints the front still from your words with the style anchor (or starts from a front you picked in front_from_picture, named by `stills`), then edits a back and a dead still from it. Wan i2v makes a 49-frame clip of each standing still 'walking in place' from your `motion` words; the loop is found by the silhouette and cut to 12 frames. The death is the `death` choice: a plain tilt into the dead still, a Wan first-last-frame fall, a driven one-shot, a squash or a collapse. You pick nothing while it runs; look at both clips and the fall afterwards and re-roll a still or a clip.
needs: the style anchor
methods.produces: 3 stills (front, back, dead), 2 clips of 12 frames, a strip of 43 columns, the icon from the front still
weaknesses: The free clip drifts: extra limbs, a face on the back, a mouth that talks; the model picks the stride count, so cycles come out doubled or halved.
The front and back clips each have their own cadence.
A blob (a slime, a tumbleweed) should not walk on a clip: it greys, its mouth moves, it grows legs; use creature_proc's hop.

A dead still 'on its back seen from above' reads as a standing T-pose from the game camera: paint it lying sideways across the frame, head left (dead_hint); a first-last-frame fall into a puddle grew legs.
'on the sand' or 'on the ground' in a prompt paints a ground patch: say no ground, no sand.
The vision QA counts no parts and judges no likeness: paint several seeds and pick the front by eye.

A green or pale sandstone creature on the green screen gets keyed or rimmed, a red glow blooms into it: screen blue. Wan picks its own clip screen (blue, green or magenta) from the figure's hues, and a blue-jeans hero once lost his legs on blue.

recipe_fields.help: What the creature is: the words the front still is painted from, with the style anchor. A look's recipe overrides the creature's own for its run.

The slug the look's paintings are cached under (<id>_<stills>_front/_back/_dead): a new look gets its own (its letter) when its job is queued; '' = the creature's own paintings; a front_from_picture pick's slug paints from that picked front.
The screen the stills are painted on and keyed off: any green in the creature, a pale sandstone one or a red glow means blue.

How much of the clip frame the figure fills (0.56 for a wide figure that touches the edge).
How much of the sprite cell the standing painting fills.
Extra words for the back still's edit (what the back shows; no face). Also the back clip's view hint.
Replaces the whole back-still prompt when the standard 'turn this exact creature around' wording fails.

recipe_fields.help: The dead still's words. Lying sideways across the frame, head left, reads best; say no ground, no sand.

Keep empty here: a look inherits every key of its creature, and an inherited pose driver would walk it on Wan Animate instead (SK-C clears it with '').

methods.name: Creature: front and back on a Mixamo stride
methods.summary: As creature_free2, but Wan Animate walks the front and back stills on a humanoid OpenPose driver (`pose` for the back, `pose_front` for the front when it differs), one sprite frame per driver frame: an exact 12-frame cadence, the same on both views. A colour flash or a foreign hue rolls a clip again, up to three seeds. With `stand: still` the idle, attack and hit frames are the painting itself; otherwise the walk's passing frame. Deaths as creature_free2, with `pose:<driver>` for a driven fall. A new driver comes from your own FBX or GLB through driver_pose.
needs: the style anchor
a 12-frame driver folder (walk, orc_walk, bigguy, walk_zombie_low/high, zombie_walk, ..., or a new one from your file)
methods.produces: 3 stills, 2 clips of 12 frames, a strip of 43 columns
weaknesses: Humanoids only: two legs, two arms, a head on top.

A still whose pose differs from the driver's (arms out, a club raised) comes out wrong: set stand still, or fit the driver with body= (the goblin on a man's skeleton came out lanky, hence orc_walk_goblin).
The driven clip falls back silently to a free clip when the figure leaves the frame or the frame check fails on odd feet (the werewolf's claws): the result's clip_kind says which; look at the clips.
The clip's first frame is the one most often wrong (the cutter keeps frames 2..n+1); a colour flash or a foreign hue re-rolls (3 seeds).
A back cycle came back with a face: back_hint.
Level arms seen from above read as hands up: arms=zombie with a per-view arm drop (walk_zombie_low for the back, walk_zombie_high for the front).
A caped or shielded figure fails the Falling Back Death driver ('figure left the frame') and tips over instead.

methods.name: Creature: eight directions, Wan guesses
methods.summary: creature_free2 plus a side, a back-diagonal and a front-diagonal still, each a Klein edit of the front with that view's own words (view_hints), and a free Wan clip for each of the five views; the game mirrors them into eight directions. Nothing to pick while it runs; five clips and six stills to look at afterwards.
needs: the style anchor
the 8-way key fix of pass 66 (before it a look with directions 8 reused or overwrote the base creature's side, bd and fd files)
methods.produces: 6 stills, 5 clips of 12 frames, a strip of 71 columns
weaknesses: Five free clips rarely share a cadence, so the views flicker against each other as the creature turns.
The side edit often comes back as a front: view_hints must spell the view out, and the QA calls an odd back view 'side'.
A scorpion's side came out on two legs; a creature with many legs wants creature_ctl, where a model decides the legs.
Everything creature_free2 says about free clips, five times over.

recipe_fields.help: 8: side, bd and fd stills and clips are made and the strip holds five views; 2: front and back only.
Per-view words for the side, back-diagonal and front-diagonal edits of the front (what shows from that side; facing screen-right).
What the creature is.

methods.name: Creature: walked on a 3D model's own motion
methods.summary: Depth videos of a rigged model (driver_depth, from your FBX or GLB: the model's own walk and death clips) drive Wan Fun Control. Stage 1 paints the side view from the model's clay render, with the style anchor first and an optional look picture (look_ref), as three candidates (Klein in 20 s each, or Flux.2 dev with --dev: the better model, 4-5 min each with a service restart) and stops for your pick. Stage 2 paints the other four views on Klein from the side painting and each view's own clay, with the way each faces spelled out (words), then walks every view along its depth video, each walk resized to its depth video's width. A wrong view is painted again as candidates (--view-cands) and picked (--use-view). The death walks the front painting along the model's death clip (death_drivers; death_keep picks its 8 frames, re-pickable without a render) or, without one, paints a dead still and Wan falls into it. The strip packs the five views into eight directions (or two with directions 2).
needs: depth drivers: tools/dl/drivers/<name>/<view>/ctl_NN.png + clay.png (driver_depth; back/ctl_24.png must exist)
optional: a death driver (front/ctl_24.png) and a look picture (look_ref)
your picks: the side candidate, then any wrong view
methods.produces: 5 stills, 5 clips of 12 frames, a strip of 71-83 columns, the icon from the front still
weaknesses: Needs a model with its own walk clip; a real creature's step can be too small to read at sprite size (driver_depth's amp swings the legs wider).
Wan keeps the painting's scale, not the video's: each view's walk is resized to its depth video's width (model_scale), so the five paintings should be the same size.
A view drifts to another colour (SC-C purple, SC-D peach): remap_hues keeps value, so a wrong colour must be repainted; keep must name the colour ('jet-black, never brown').
The anatomy words are the creature's: the scorpion's 'exactly one tail' once went to every creature.
A floating sting or horn: drop_islands and another walk seed for that view (walk_seeds).
The death roll smears in the middle: death_keep picks the frames that read.
A Klein 'dead on its back' still came out as a live scorpion rearing up and the vision check passed it: use the model's death clip.
A plain or simple look on Flux.2 dev returns the clay itself: edit a richer look instead.
Flux.2 dev restarts the ComfyUI service before every render and cannot run in batches; the third dev render in one process once sat 30 minutes.
A front painted from the blockout came out top-down with the head at the far end: the side is painted first for a reason.

The look: what the creature is painted as (the side candidates' words).

The death clip's words.

Key hues near the screen's green out of the figure.
Playback rate of the walks in the game.

The screen the views are painted on.

methods.name: Creature: no video at all
methods.summary: The painting itself moves. `walk: hop` squashes and stretches it along a little parabola (hop_height; cell_fill gives it headroom), or --no-video leans and bobs it for a six-frame walk. The death is squash (into the puddle), collapse (slices dropping into a painted heap) or a plain tilt into the dead still. Three Klein stills (front, back, dead), no clip, and nothing can go wrong with the face or the colours. The quickest method, and the one for anything without legs.
needs: the style anchor
methods.produces: 3 stills, 0 clips, a strip (a hop of 12 frames, or a 6-frame walk)
weaknesses: Reads as a cut-out: only for blobs, tumbleweeds, things without legs.
collapse needs a dead_hint that describes a heap: a painted mid-collapse came out as a two-headed skeleton.
Raise the creature's size to keep its on-screen size when cell_fill gives the hop headroom.

recipe_fields.help: What the creature is.
The slug the look's paintings are cached under: a new look gets its own (its letter); '' = the creature's own; a front_from_picture slug paints from that picked front.
hop: a 12-frame squash-and-stretch hop from the painting; '': with the job's no_video a 6-frame lean-and-bob walk.
How high the hop goes, as a fraction of the cell.
How much of the cell the painting fills (headroom for the hop; raise the creature's size to keep it the same on screen).
squash: the painting squashes into the puddle; collapse: slices drop into the painted heap; '': a tilt into the dead still.

recipe_fields.default: lying flat on its back on the ground, dead: eyes shut tight, tongue hanging out, limbs sprawled limp in the air
recipe_fields.help: The dead still's words (for a collapse, describe the heap).
The screen the stills are painted on (a green slime goes on blue).
Extra words for the back still.
Outline width as a fraction of the cell.
Outline colour, hex.
The sprite cell in pixels.
Keyer saturation threshold.
Keyer value threshold.
Keyer: cut the bottom shadow band.

Keep empty: no driver, no clip.

methods.name: Front painting from a picture (a pre-step)
methods.summary: Klein redraws your 2D picture as the house style's front still: the picture flattened on white goes in as a reference (after the style anchor, unless no_style_ref makes it the only one) with the 'redraw this exact creature' wording (identity, followed closely), N seeds, a review sheet. You pick one; it is copied to <id>_<slug>_front and becomes the `stills` key any creature method paints the back and dead from. The picture reaches the front only: everything else is an edit of that painting.
needs: a picture under the repo (an upload, or _REFERENCES/2d/...)
weaknesses: Identity holds only as well as Klein edits; the back and the dead are Klein's guesses from the front.
A character copied as a Klein edit on the green screen lost its talons on the back (boots instead): name the feet in words.
The vision QA judges no likeness: pick by eye.
A green subject on the green screen is keyed away: screen blue.

recipe_fields.help: The slug the pick writes into the look's recipe (wwa, wwb, ...): the stills are cached as <id>_<slug>_front/_back/_dead.

job_fields.help: The 2D picture (png/jpg/webp under the repo).
What it is, in the house style's words ('a hunched werewolf with torn trousers').
How many candidates to paint (about 20 s each).
The screen the candidates are painted on.
Appended as 'Keep <keep>.' (the thing the redraw must not lose).

No model runs. The server copies the source look's anims, strip_cols, fps and head into the new entry; a preview sheet shows the result first.

A hue range that touches the outline, the eyes or the weapon recolours them too: look at the preview.

Hue ranges (0-360) to move; several allowed.
The hue the ranges' middle moves to.
Saturation multiplier on the moved pixels.
hue: move the hues; tint: a pale material made dark and saturated (set_sat, value, min_val).

methods.name: Item icon (one roll)

The old icon is backed up first. For a shape that matters, paint candidates instead (icon_cands) with a render of the real thing.
needs: an art_prompt on the item
weaknesses: One roll, no reference: for a gun, dice or a guitar use icon_cands with a Blender render copied exactly.
Any green in the subject means the blue screen, or the keyer eats it.
A glow asked for in the prompt keys into a green halo.
Flux bends dice and gun barrels: render the true shape and copy it.

recipe_fields.help: The one bold object to paint, in plain words (the Shop Titans style words are added).
The screen it is painted on (the placeholder colour steers it when unset; green subjects go on blue).

methods.name: Icon candidates (pick by eye)
methods.summary: N seeds of the icon prompt (the subject, the Shop Titans icon words, the screen), with one reference picture laid on the screen colour. The server fills what you leave empty (pass 68): a creature's subject is its description (its appearance, else its art_prompt without the still's pose) and its reference the look's own front still, so the icon is this creature; an item's subject is its art_prompt and its reference its 3D render when there is one (tools/dl/<id>_ref.png). With a reference on a creature the words begin 'The reference image shows this exact creature: keep its shape, colors and proportions.'; for an item write the copy wording yourself ('Copy this exact object from the reference image: ...'). --dev paints on Flux.2 dev (8 Turbo steps, 28 with Turbo off; 4-5 min a seed, a service restart each). Every attempt paints its own candidates (a re-run never hands back the old ones). A review sheet; you pick one and it is installed (the old one backed up under tools/dl/backup): an item's icon, a creature's, or a creature look's <id>_icon_<x>.png and its entry's icon. A hero's icon is the round badge: hero_badge.
needs: optional: a reference render (ref_render's icon_ref.png) or a picture under tools/dl
methods.produces: tools/dl/icons_le_<job>[_a<attempt>]/<key>_c<k>.png and review_<key>.png; the pick installs the icon
weaknesses: Counts parts wrong (an extra barrel, six strings on a four-string): pick by eye.
Any green in the subject means the blue screen.
Grey and silver pick up the screen's tint and the keyer cuts them (the magnet's caps): key with cut_shadow off and the screen clamped.
A plain or simple look on Flux.2 dev returns the reference itself.
A glow in the prompt keys into a halo; gold reads tan unless deep and a little self-lit.

job_fields.help: What to paint. Empty = filled by the server: a creature's description (appearance, else art_prompt without the pose), an item's art_prompt. Nothing is put in front of it for an item: to have a render copied exactly, begin with 'Copy this exact object from the reference image: its silhouette, proportions, parts and colours, seen from the same angle.'

The one reference picture, laid on the screen colour (no style anchor for icons): a repo path (tools/dl/uploads/2d/<file>), a tools/dl path or an absolute one. Empty = the creature look's own front still, an item's 3D render.
The screen colour (blue for anything with green in it). Empty = the creature's or item's own screen, else the one gen_art paints it on.
Replaces the Shop Titans style words (UI art, badges).
The icon file the pick writes. Empty = a look's <id>_icon_<x>.png, else the icon the game reads (<id>_icon.png).
How many candidates.
Flux.2 dev instead of Klein: 8 Turbo steps, 28 with Turbo off (better, 4-5 min a seed, one service restart each).

The server fills every field you leave empty, so the badge is this hero. Every job paints its own candidates (<id>_portrait_<tag>_c<k>: a new job never hands back old pictures). You pick one: for the hero it becomes <id>_icon.png and badge.still in the hero's JSON (so a later base run keeps it); for a look (variant) it becomes <id>_icon_<x>.png and that look's icon.

Room above the head inside the circle.

'hit' in a prompt paints impact rings.

The pose of the splash. Empty = title_pose, else the tool's own table, else 'standing confidently in a heroic pose, full body'.
The one thing held ('the guitar is the only thing he holds'). Empty = title_holds, else the tool's table, else 'no weapon'.
The shot. Empty = title_camera, else 'facing the viewer, seen from the front at eye level'.
The identity picture. Empty = the look's own front still, else the hero's; any picture path, or an upload.
A second picture copied exactly, e.g. a render of the held object (title_extra_ref.file).

The look the cut-out is for (filled from the target's code): its pick writes art/ui/wanted/hero_<id>_<x>.png and that look's title; empty = the hero's own.
How many candidates (each on its own seed: a million apart, moved by the job's id and by every re-run; pass 70).
The first seed.

methods.name: New OpenPose driver from an FBX or GLB
methods.summary: pose_driver.py reads the armature of your file (a Mixamo-style FBX; a GLB with Mixamo names; Cinema 4D's Bone_SM_* names with rig=sm; any other humanoid with a bone map, which the probe guesses for you to check) and resamples one stride to N frames for the five game views, seen from a camera pitched 25 degrees down, then draws them as OpenPose skeletons with 21-point hands and a contact sheet per view. 24 frames for a hero run, 12 for a creature walk; loop off for a one-shot such as a death (N of 4k+1: 9, 25); start and end in seconds slice one stride out of a longer clip. Options: arms zombie or hold_r, body= to fit a creature's proportions, fwd=body for a toe-out walk. The fitted copies for a hero come from hero_fit's pre-steps.
needs: an FBX or GLB with a humanoid rig and one clip (ref_probe says whether, and lists the clips)
weaknesses: A rig with other bone names needs rigmap= (the probe's guess, checked in the bone-map form); a missing bone stops it.
A clip with several strides must be sliced to one (start, end).
A man's skeleton makes a goblin lanky: body= fits the proportions read off the painting.
Wide arms leave the clip frame: pose_scale 0.85 on the back views; toe-out feet turn the views up to 20 degrees: fwd=body.
The hands are drawn only from a full finger chain (Mixamo's); the zombie's three-joint fingers draw none.

job_fields.help: The FBX or GLB (an upload under tools/dl/uploads/3d, or a file under the repo).
The driver folder's name under tools/dl/drivers.
Frames per view: 24 for a hero run, 12 for a creature walk; a one-shot wants 4k+1 (9, 25).
A loop (the last frame repeats the first) or a one-shot.
Seconds into the clip where the stride (or the one-shot) starts.
Seconds where it ends (0: the clip's end).
The camera's tilt down, degrees (the game's 25).

zombie: both arms held out in front (arm_drop degrees down); hold_r: the right hand holds something up at the shoulder; back (pass 69): both arms swept straight back behind the body, arm_drop 40 below the horizontal (the dash, Jezyk's run).
zombie arms: how far they slope down, degrees (level arms seen from above read as hands up).
Proportions read off the painting as fractions of its height: top_nose:0.21,nose_neck:0.134,torso:0.292,thigh:0.16,shin:0.14,shoulder:0.119,hip:0.068,upper:0.174,fore:0.139,hand:0.078 (the goblin).
Where 'forward' is read from: the feet (toe minus ankle) or the hip and shoulder lines (toe-out walks).
The bone-name table: Mixamo's names, or Cinema 4D's Bone_SM_*.
The bone map for another humanoid rig ({model bone: Mixamo name}, or the probe's {Mixamo name: model bone}); saved as rigmap.json beside the upload.
Which clip when the file holds several (the probe lists them).
Pass 69: the limbs swing this many times as far round their average rotation, baked into the clip (1.35 on the legs + lean 12 = run_sprint).
A regex over the bones amp applies to (empty: (Arm|ForeArm|UpLeg|Leg)$, the limbs).
Pass 69: the spine bent forward this many degrees in all (a third at each of Spine, Spine1, Spine2): 12 a sprint, 14 the dash.

Pass 69 (tools/pose_shoulders.py): level the shoulders with the neck: each shoulder's height off the neck times this (0.3), the arms moving with them, written as a second driver <name>_lvl. The Mixamo Neck sits above the shoulder line, so without it Wan paints sagging shoulders from behind and a hunched near shoulder in the side passing frames. Empty: off.
The views it levels: back,bd for the back driver; side,fd (with tuck) for the side driver.

Side view: the far upper arm turns to at most this many degrees back from straight down in the frames where the near arm is swung back (25); its elbow up behind the back read as a raised shoulder. Empty: off.

runner.then: with shoulders: python tools/pose_shoulders.py tools/dl/drivers/{name} tools/dl/drivers/{name}_lvl level={shoulders} views={shoulder_views} tuck={tuck}?

methods.name: Depth drivers from a rigged model's own clip
methods.summary: blender_depth_drivers.py plays the clip you choose on the model (any rig: a beetle, a scorpion, a humanoid), takes the travel out per frame, optionally swings the leg bones wider (amp), and writes for each of the five game views a depth video (near bright, far dark, 25 frames: 12 x 2 cycles + 1), a clay render and a textured look render; mode oneshot for a death or an attack (the front view, 25 frames evenly over the clip, with clay thumbnails at the quarters). Clay first, so a bad framing shows before the depth frames. The folder is what creature_ctl's drivers / death_drivers name. Ten seconds for the beetle.
needs: an FBX or GLB with an armature and a clip (ref_probe lists the clips: a walk, a death, an idle)
methods.produces: tools/dl/drivers/<name>/<view>/ctl_00..24.png, clay.png, look.png (+ clay_NN.png for a one-shot), meta.json (kind depth)
weaknesses: The framing is per model (three extents away, 1.45 extents wide): look at clay.png first.
A real creature's step can be too small to read at sprite size: amp swings the matching bones wider, and the leg bones' names must match amp_bones (the beetle's unnamed legs needed ^Bone\.00[345]).
A wide depth range leaves the far legs flat and Wan walks them on nothing: depth tight (the default) and Raw frames.
Do not lay a model on its side for readability; a mirrored or oddly facing model needs forward= set.
A clip with root motion is held on the spot by its box centre, which also removes a real lunge; inplace=0 keeps it.

job_fields.help: The FBX, GLB/glTF, OBJ, DAE, .blend or a zip of one.
The driver folder's name under tools/dl/drivers.
The clip: its exact name, the part after the last '|' (walk, death) or a unique piece of it.
cycle: a looping walk (frames x cycles + 1); oneshot: a death or attack played once over `total` frames.
cycle: poses per stride.
cycle: strides in the video (12 x 2 + 1 = 25, Wan's 4k+1).
oneshot: frames over the clip.
Seconds into the clip where the stride starts (slices a longer clip).
Seconds where it ends (0: the clip's end).
tight: each view's own depth range (the lesson of pass 49); wide: one range for all views.
Swing the matching bones this much wider round their average pose (1.7 for the beetle).
A regex over bone names for amp (the probe lists the names).
The camera's tilt down, degrees.
Which views (a one-shot: front).
The way the model faces (-Y is Blender's and the beetle's); auto takes the probe's guess.
The clay and look renders' background.
A colour map for look.png when the file's own texture paths are missing (a sibling textures/ folder is found by itself).
Take the travel out per frame (cycles); a one-shot keeps it unless set.

methods.name: A driver tweaked: one view scaled, hands kept out, hands hidden, shoulders levelled
methods.summary: A copy of a driver from the library with one change in chosen views, drawn again, so one view of a look can be walked again on it (Re-roll... on the look, its clip ticked, the recipe naming the new driver for that view). scale: every keypoint of the views moves toward the clip's middle by `scale` (0.85 keeps wide arms or a hat inside the clip's frame); it does not change the sprite's size: gen_art fits every walk back to the standing height, so a view too tall or too small against the others is the look's `run_scale` (Run size per view in its recipe), not a driver. spread: in the back views a wrist inside the torso's width is pushed out past it (hands painted on a back or through the clothes). occlude: in the back views a wrist inside the torso is dropped (the model then paints no hand there). shoulders: the shoulders levelled with the neck (`level` 0.3; `tuck` turns the side view's far arm down behind the torso). Seconds, no model, no ComfyUI.
needs: a pose driver in tools/dl/drivers (meta.json kind pose): run, run_side, run_spread_lvl, walk, catwalk_fit, ...
methods.produces: tools/dl/drivers/<name>/<view>/driver_NN.png and poses.json, <view>_sheet.png, all_sheet.png, meta.json (a copy of the source's, kind pose)
weaknesses: One change a job: chain jobs for two (spread a copy, then level the copy's shoulders); the new name must be free.

scale moves the skeleton inside the frame; gen_art scales each clip back to the standing still's height, so a whole view that comes out too small or too tall is fixed by the look's run_scale (Run size: <view> in its recipe; nothing painted again), never by a scaled driver.
spread and occlude look at the back views only (back, bd): hands through the clothes on a front view want a driver whose front arms swing beside the body, or the hint words.
The tools do not check the result: look at the new driver's sheets (the job card shows all_sheet.png) before you walk a look on it.

job_fields.help: The driver to start from (a folder under tools/dl/drivers).
The new driver's folder name (a free one: run_spread_lvl_s90).
scale (shrink or grow chosen views), spread (back wrists out past the torso), occlude (back wrists inside the torso dropped), shoulders (level them with the neck; tuck for the side's far arm).
op scale: how far every keypoint moves toward the clip's middle (0.85 = 15 % smaller; above 1 grows it).
op scale and shoulders: the views changed (front, fd, side, bd, back; comma-separated).
op spread: how far past the torso's edge a wrist goes (of the frame's width).
op shoulders: each shoulder's height off the neck times this (0 = level with the neck, 1 = unchanged).
op shoulders, side view: the far upper arm at most this many degrees back from straight down (25); empty = off.

runner.then: op spread: python tools/pose_spread.py src dst spread={spread}; op occlude: python tools/pose_occlude.py src dst; op shoulders: python tools/pose_shoulders.py src dst level={level} views={views} tuck={tuck}?

methods.name: What a 3D file can do
methods.summary: blender_ref.py reads the file (FBX, GLB/glTF, OBJ, DAE, .blend, or a zip holding one the way Sketchfab packs them) and writes probe.json: the armatures with their bone names, the clips with their length in frames and seconds, the meshes and whether they carry textures, the size (a centimetre model is scaled to metres), a rig guess (Mixamo, Cinema 4D sm, other, none) with a 21-row bone-map guess for an unknown humanoid, where the model faces, and which uses it allows: the icon, the look, pose drivers, depth drivers; with a sentence saying so. Plus thumbs.png: the five game views and the icon's angle at 192 px. A few seconds.
needs: the uploaded file
weaknesses: The forward guess reads a humanoid's feet (a toe-out walk reads up to 20 degrees off) and defaults to -Y for everything else: check thumbs.png.
The bone-map guess is by name; a rig with cryptic names (Bone.003_L) maps nothing and takes the form by hand.
A Collada (.dae) file needs this Blender's importer; export FBX or GLB when it fails.

job_fields.help: The model file or zip.
The way the model faces, for the thumbs.
The clip to pose the thumbs on (default the armature's own, or the first).
Seconds into the clip for the thumbs' pose.
auto: a model taller than 20 units is scaled x0.01; or a factor.

methods.name: Icon and look renders of a 3D model
methods.summary: mode icon: a 1024 px front-left three-quarter from a little above (icon_yaw 35 degrees round from the front toward the model's left, icon_pitch 20: the angle of tools/dl/tommy_ref.png), orthographic, textured when the model has textures, on a transparent film (the icon pipeline lays it on green or blue itself): the reference icon_cands copies exactly. mode views: the five game views as warm clay (clay.png) and in the model's own colours (look.png), framed exactly like the depth drivers: the look reference creature_ctl's look_ref names, or a picture for front_from_picture. Posed on the clip and moment you choose.
needs: the uploaded file (ref_probe first, to know its clips and which way it faces)
methods.produces: icon_ref.png (1024 px, transparent); <view>/clay.png and <view>/look.png (640 px) for front, fd, side, bd, back
weaknesses: The framing is automatic (the projected box, 10 percent margin): a long thin object fills the width, a tall one the height.
A model without textures renders in its material colours; a Sketchfab FBX whose texture paths are gone needs albedo= (a sibling textures/ folder is found by itself).
A model that faces +X or +Y comes out turned unless forward= says so (the probe's thumbs show it).

A colour map for the textured renders.

ref_note: There is no strength number: references steer by which pictures go in, in what order, and these words. A Klein render takes its references as ReferenceLatents only (comfy.py:277-285): no strength, no denoise, no IP-Adapter; keep to at most four references (a practice rule, unverified in code). A 2D picture reaches only the front still of a creature (front_from_picture) or the side of a creature_ctl look (look_ref); every other view is an edit of that painting. Motion is never steered by a picture: Wan takes the still and words, or drivers. The seed and the reference order are the only other levers. The vision QA checks count, background and view, never likeness: pick by eye.
insert_3d_text: Preferred: a Mixamo-style FBX Binary, 30 fps, 'In Place' ticked, keyframe reduction none, with skin; or a GLB that carries its animation with a known rig (Mixamo bone names, or Cinema 4D's Bone_SM_*). A model without an animation clip can still be the icon's reference and the look reference, but cannot drive a walk. After the upload the probe reads the file and the editor offers what fits: (1) a Mixamo-style humanoid with a clip: pose drivers (24 frames for a hero run, 12 for a creature walk; a loop, or a one-shot with start and end; pitch, arms, fwd) and depth drivers, both; (2) Bone_SM_Pelvis: the same with rig=sm; (3) another armature with a clip: the bone-map form (the probe's 21-row guess, saved as rigmap.json) and then pose drivers, or depth drivers; (4) an armature with a clip that is not a humanoid: depth drivers only, with the clips listed to choose the walk, the death, the idle; (5) no clip: the icon and look renders only ('This model has no animation clip, so it cannot drive a walk; it can be the icon's reference and the look reference. For a walk export it from Mixamo as FBX Binary, 30 fps, In Place, keyframe reduction none, or a GLB that carries its animation.'); (6) no armature and no mesh: not a model Blender can read. Per reference you tick what it is for: the icon (ref_render's icon_ref.png as icon_cands' reference), the look (the side clay or look render as creature_ctl's look_ref, or a picture for front_from_picture), the animation (driver_pose or driver_depth).
timings_note: Medians measured on disk (417 cached cycle.json files, pass 66 findings 1.13): a Klein still about 20 s; a Flux.2 dev render at 28 steps 205-286 s plus a service restart of about 20 s each; a Wan Animate (pose) clip of 25 frames 55 s (32-578 s on a loaded server); a Fun Control walk 93 s, a one-shot 86 s; a first-last-frame fall 132 s; a free i2v clip of 49 frames 151 s; the LM Studio QA about 8 s a still when it is up. Blender, measured this pass on the beetle and a Mixamo FBX: a probe 2-4 s; the icon and the five clay + look views 4 s; depth drivers 10 s for five views (125 Cycles frames at 4 samples), 4 s for a one-shot; a pose driver 4 s in Blender plus 3 s to draw. Godot after a landing: --import (plus lossy_imports and a second --import) and import_json, 1-3 minutes under the Godot lock. The estimates are medians: a client timeout (3600 s) leaves a Wan job running on the server, and Flux.2 dev once sat 30 minutes loading into a full RAM.
